item.title: [BBC World] COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
item.description:
Image source, ReutersByMark Poynting, Esme Stallard and Justin RowlattBBC Climate and SciencePublished22 November 2026Updated 1 hour ago
Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.
Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.
But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.
Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures.
The last time a COP's main political agreement collapsed like this was in 2009 in Copenhagen.
UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, in his last COP before he steps down, said he was "deeply disappointed".
He took aim at what he called "powerful fossil fuel interests" who he said were taking "a page from Big Tobacco's playbook: distorting the science, delaying policy, blocking action, and piling up huge profits while people everywhere pay the price".
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the talks, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".
"That is the reality," he said on Monday.
After two weeks of negotiations, exhausted delegates were presented with a new, draft deal in the early hours of Sunday to try to break the deadlock.
But the words "fossil fuels" did not appear anywhere in the text. The only indirect reference to coal, oil and gas was a nod to a deal agreed at COP28 in 2023, when countries agreed to "transition away" from fossil fuels in energy systems.
The EU's representative, Irish Minister Darragh O'Brien, made it clear that the EU "strongly" objected, saying that the "decisions go nowhere near the le...

Douala, Cameroon – Collins Mbah says he hunted down and killed several Cameroonian soldiers in the English-speaking Northwest region during his time as a separatist fighter between 2016 and 2020. Today, in the coastal city of Douala, the man in his mid-30s, who went by the name Commander No Sorrow, has taken on a different role: traditional healer, tending to lives rather than taking them.
Mbah says he abandoned the armed struggle after realising that fellow fighters were turning against the very people they had set out to protect. But he has firmly ruled out joining the government’s disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration (DDR) programme.
“Quitting the struggle and joining the government disarmament programme would have meant I betrayed the people,” said Mbah, who dropped out of secondary school to join the revolt. “I don’t want to have anything to do with the government or the struggle any more. All I need now is peace of mind,” he told Al Jazeera.
October marked a decade since protests erupted in Cameroon’s English-speaking Northwest and Southwest regions, eventually escalating into an armed conflict between separatist fighters and government forces.
The unrest began in late 2016 after Anglophone lawyers and teachers protested against the appointment of Francophone magistrates unfamiliar with British common law to courts in English-speaking regions, and French-speaking teachers unable to communicate fluently in English to schools there. Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack
No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia
A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.
The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.
Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press.
View image in fullscreen
Aerial view of the Russian naval vessel Merkury before it was struck in the port of Benghazi, Libya, 21 November 2026. Photograph: 2026 Vantor/EPA
Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine, marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war.
Though Ukraine began the war with no navy, it has developed a sea drone capability that threatened Russian warships in the Black Sea. The Russian fleet has been forced to retreat to the eastern port of Novorossiysk because Sevastopol in occupied Crimea had become unsafe.

An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.
The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libya state media reported, citing the eastern government.
The statement said there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.
Later on Sunday, the health ministry said it had received injured people from another vessel, a commercial ship, that was also targeted off the coast of Benghazi, state media reported. Their injuries were minor and their condition stable, the ministry said.
Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also shows a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port.
Image source, Planet Labs PBCImage caption,
Satellite imagery showed a ship on fire at the port
US-based intelligence firm Vantor collected high-resolution images that it said showed Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette (Merkury) - a Russian navy ship - moored in the port on Saturday, and on Sunday showed most of the same ship capsized and sunk with only the forward bow still visible.
The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) said the Russian ship - which it did not name or identify - was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.
Sunday's incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.

The sea drone strike triggered an explosion and fire in Benghazi.BySAMY MAGDY Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 10:28 AM

CAIRO -- A suspected Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship Sunday at a naval base in Libya, officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.
The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said.
They said that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, they said.

A U.N.-supported government is based in Tripoli and a rival administration is located in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.
The eastern Libya-based government said in a statement that the strike Sunday caused an explosion and fire at the base, which was later extinguished.
The Almasar satellite television channel aired footage showing a vessel erupting into flames. It said the Libyan navy rescued the crew of the Maltese-flagged ship. A corvette warship is smaller than a frigate or destroyer and is built to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.

item.title: [ABC News World] Poland says Russia twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper
item.description:
Poland says Russia twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper
Denmark expelled a Russian official after it said it thwarted an alleged plot.ByCLAUDIA CIOBANU Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 1:12 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
WARSAW, Poland -- Denmark has expelled a Russian official after it said it had thwarted an alleged plot to kill a Ukrainian American citizen on Danish soil. The case took a new twist Sunday when Polish authorities revealed that the same man was allegedly targeted by Moscow's intelligence services last summer in Poland.
Denmark is expected to ask the European Union this week for more decisive action stemming from the case, perhaps restricting Russian citizens from entering and traveling freely within the EU. Poland said it would support such measures.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Russia’s threats were becoming more real, reaching EU soil as the bloc continues supporting Ukraine as Moscow's full-scale invasion nears the five-year mark.
The case involves Albert Vasiliev, a rapper who performs under the name Kyivstoner and holds Ukrainian and U.S. citizenship, according to Danish media.
The assassination attempt in Denmark was planned for Sept. 25 during a concert north of Copenhagen, according to the Danish Security and Intelligence Service, known by its acronym PET. It said the plot was “planned and initiated by Russian intelligence services.”
The plot was thwarted by authorities, the Danish prime minister’s office said Friday. PET said two men were charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service in operating in Denmark. They were linked to Loyal to Familia, it said, a banned gang known for “extensive, serious and violent criminal activity.”
Russia dismissed the allegations through its embassy in Copenhagen, saying the accusations were unsubstantiated.
Denmark responded by expelling Russia’s defense attaché.

item.description:
The BYD Fangchengbao 7, known as the Ti7 in some export markets, is displayed during the Beijing Auto Show in April this year. Photograph: Adek Berry/AFP/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
The BYD Fangchengbao 7, known as the Ti7 in some export markets, is displayed during the Beijing Auto Show in April this year. Photograph: Adek Berry/AFP/Getty Images
Court bans China’s BYD from selling ‘Defender clone’ SUV in EU
District court in the Hague finds Chinese carmaker infringed on intellectual property of Jaguar Land Rover
Chinese carmaker BYD has been banned from selling its “Defender clone” vehicle in the EU by a court in the Netherlands, after Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) brought a case saying it infringed intellectual property rights.
JLR launched legal action over the seven-seater Ti7 SUV earlier this year after BYD announced on its website that it was taking orders from UK customers for the vehicle. Earlier this month, bailiffs acting for JLR were reported to have seized digital records from BYD’s offices.
“In these summary proceedings, the preliminary relief judge rules that ​the Ti7 infringes the EU design of Jaguar Land Rover,” said the ruling from the district court in The Hague. “The characteristic ⁠and distinctive elements of the design are reflected in the BYD Ti7.”

item.title: [CBS News World] U.N. climate summit ends without deal after contentious fossil fuel debate
item.description:
COP31, the United Nations' annual climate conference, ended Sunday without a final agreement after days of contentious talks collapsed, mainly because of disputes between nations pushing to phase out fossil fuel use and others opposed to doing so.
The breakdown capped two weeks of negotiations in Antalya, Turkey, between delegations from nearly 200 countries. Their debates ran into overtime, becoming the longest COP summit in history, at a moment that U.N. officials and many scientists have called decisive for the trajectory of global warming and climate change.
U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres said in a statement that Sunday he was "deeply disappointed" by the outcome of the summit.
"I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," he said. "But this setback does not change the facts. There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science."
The United States sent no representatives to the climate conference for the second year in a row, following the Trump administration's withdrawal from the 2015 Paris Agreement. That accord set a goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above preindustrial levels, a target that has anchored every U.N. climate summit since and that the world is now poised to overshoot.
Talks reached an impasse Sunday, as the European Union opposed a draft agreement that failed to mention fossil fuels and which, its delegates argued, placated countries that export them.
"We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuel, which is the key driver of climate change," said Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU in Antalya. "And we will not accept negotiating backward in time, and we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel."

The governor of Kaliningrad says a rare air alert sounded in the Russian exclave near Poland and LithuaniaByThe Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 7:14 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
KYIV, Ukraine -- A rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there.
The alert late Saturday in Kaliningrad came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, which is a key base for Russia's Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday.
Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed. But The Associated Press couldn't immediately verify the authenticity of the images.
According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022.
The Kaliningrad governor, Alexei Bezprozvannykh, said that “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 kilometers (105 miles) northeast of Baltiysk.
On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defenses working there during the night. They featured photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky, with crackling sounds heard in the background.
Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, that showed clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, while an orange haze glowed on the horizon. They told Russian state media that the photo “had nothing to do with the region.”

California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded
Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.
Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

item.description:

The $75,000 reward offered by Chen Jie's family has sparked fears of more reckless climbing attemptsByKelly NgPublished20 November 2026
The Chinese embassy in Japan has warned its citizens against off-season ascents of Mount Fuji amid concerns that the hefty reward offered by a missing hiker's family could encourage more reckless climbing.
Chen Jie, 25, vanished on 8 November on the mountain. His family is offering 500,000 yuan ($75,000; £57,300) to anyone who finds him alive, and 100,000 yuan to anyone who recovers his body, say Chinese and Japanese media reports.
Strong winds and blizzards pose serious risks during the closed season, especially as shelter and first-aid centres are not operational, the embassy said on Tuesday.
Mount Fuji's official climbing season runs from around early July to early September.
Earlier this year, authorities of Yamanashi province, where the northern part of Mount Fuji sits, had said that people who attempt to climb Mount Fuji during off-peak seasons and then require rescue by helicopter will have to pay for the service from next year on.
Authorities will also require those looking to scale Fuji during the off-season to submit detailed climbing plans.
"We hope that these measures will cause people to rethink what climbing Mount Fuji during the winter is like," Kotaro Nagasaki, the prefecture governor, said at the time.
On Wednesday, Nagasaki told reporters that attempts to find the missing climber could lead to "secondary disasters".
According to Japanese news outlet the Mainichi Shimbun, Nagasaki appeared to appeal to Chen's family, saying: "I understand that your family is important, but please refrain from doing anything that could endanger others."
Some social media users in Japan have similarly expressed fears would entice people to venture into the mountains ill-prepared and lead to more accidents.

Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits
Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.
The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer.
The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago, when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park, owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. Ivanishvili has filled the park with ancient, giant trees from Georgia, transporting them by boat along the Black Sea.
The export of the Kenyan baobabs was initially blocked after an outcry by environmentalists, who condemned their export as biopiracy, but later allowed to go ahead.
